questions.q: The 1's complement of the 8-bit number 10110010 is
questions.e: The 1's complement just inverts every bit: 10110010 becomes 01001101. Adding 1 would give the 2's complement.

questions.q: The 8-bit 2's complement representation of the number −20 is
questions.e: 20 = 00010100. Its 1's complement is 11101011, and adding 1 gives 11101100.

questions.q: The BCD (8421) code of the decimal number 47 is
questions.e: Each decimal digit is coded separately in 4 bits: 4 = 0100 and 7 = 0111. 1011 is not a valid BCD digit.

questions.q: The Gray code equivalent of the binary number 1011 is
questions.e: Keep the MSB, then XOR adjacent bits: 1, 1⊕0 = 1, 0⊕1 = 1, 1⊕1 = 0, giving 1110.

questions.q: The excess-3 code of the decimal digit 7 is
questions.e: Excess-3 is the BCD of the digit plus 3: 7 + 3 = 10 = 1010.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about standard ASCII is NOT correct?
o: Extended ASCII uses 8 bits per character
questions.e: Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code with 2⁷ = 128 characters. The 256-character set is extended 8-bit ASCII.

questions.q:
Regarding logic gates, consider the following statements.
I. A NAND gate alone can be used to build any other logic gate.
II. A NOR gate alone can be used to build any other logic gate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. NAND and NOR are universal gates, since AND, OR and NOT can each be built from either one alone.

questions.q: The output of a two-input XOR gate is 1 only when its inputs are ______.
questions.e: XOR gives 1 for 01 and 10, and 0 for 00 and 11. So it detects inequality of the inputs.

questions.q: The output of a two-input NOR gate is HIGH only when
o: at least one input is HIGH
questions.e: NOR is an OR followed by NOT, so it gives 1 only for input 00.

questions.q: A NOT gate can be obtained from a two-input NAND gate by
o: connecting the output to one input
questions.e: NAND(A, A) = (A·A)' = A'. Tying one input to 0 would force the output to 1.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements based on De Morgan's theorems.
I. (A + B)' = A' + B'
II. (A · B)' = A' · B'
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. De Morgan's laws are (A + B)' = A'·B' and (A·B)' = A' + B'. The operator changes when the complement is distributed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about binary codes.
I. Gray code is a weighted code.
II. Excess-3 code is a weighted code.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is weighted. Gray code is an unweighted, unit-distance code, and excess-3 is an unweighted, self-complementing code. BCD 8421 is the weighted one.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about a four-variable Karnaugh map is NOT correct?
o: Adjacent cells differ in exactly one variable
Rows and columns are labelled in ordinary binary order 00, 01, 10, 11
questions.e: The labels follow Gray code order 00, 01, 11, 10, so that neighbouring cells differ in one variable only. The map has 2⁴ = 16 cells, one per minterm.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a half adder.
I. Its carry output is A ⊕ B.
II. Its sum output is A ⊕ B.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. Sum = A ⊕ B and carry = A·B. A carry is produced only when both input bits are 1.

questions.q: How many select lines are required for an 8-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.e: With n select lines a multiplexer chooses among 2ⁿ inputs, so 2ⁿ = 8 gives n = 3.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about decoders and encoders.
I. A decoder with n inputs has up to 2ⁿ outputs.
II. An encoder with 2ⁿ inputs has n outputs.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. A 3-to-8 decoder has 8 outputs, and an 8-to-3 encoder has 3 outputs.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid behaviour of a JK flip-flop on a clock pulse?
o: J = 1, K = 1: the output is undefined
J = 0, K = 0: the output stays unchanged
J = 0, K = 1: the output is reset to 0
J = 1, K = 0: the output is set to 1
questions.e: With J = K = 1 the JK flip-flop toggles, so the next state is Q'. It is the SR flip-flop that has an invalid input combination.

questions.q:
Regarding a NOR-based SR latch, consider the following statements.
I. The input combination S = R = 1 is not allowed.
II. With S = R = 0, the latch retains its previous state.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. S = R = 1 forces both outputs to 0 and the final state is unpredictable when released. S = R = 0 simply holds the state.

questions.q: The characteristic equation of a D flip-flop is
questions.e: The D flip-flop copies the D input to the output on the active clock edge.

questions.q: A 6-bit shift register requires ______ flip-flops.
questions.e: A register stores one bit per flip-flop, so 6 bits need 6 flip-flops.

questions.q: The minimum number of flip-flops needed to build a modulo-16 counter is
questions.e: Modulus ≤ 2ⁿ, so n = log₂16 = 4.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a volatile memory?
questions.e: ROM keeps its contents without power. SRAM, DRAM and registers lose data when power is removed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about memory chips.
I. The contents of an EPROM are erased electrically.
II. The contents of an EEPROM are erased electrically.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. An EPROM has a quartz window and is erased by exposure to ultraviolet light. An EEPROM is erased by electrical signals.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about logic families.
I. ECL is the fastest of the common logic families.
II. CMOS dissipates more static power than TTL.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: ECL avoids saturation and is the fastest. CMOS has very low static power dissipation, so statement II is false.

questions.q: An analog-to-digital converter (ADC)
o: converts a binary number into a voltage
converts a continuous voltage into a binary number
converts serial data into parallel data
questions.e: An ADC samples an analog signal and gives the digital code. The reverse job belongs to a DAC.

questions.q: Which of the following gives the correct full form of TTL?
questions.e: TTL is built with bipolar junction transistors in both the input and the output stages.
